[link preview]Resolution criteria

This market resolves to YES if Andrew Tate is physically detained in a jail, prison, or correctional holding facility continuously (or being transferred) in any jurisdiction (including the United States, the United Kingdom, Romania, or elsewhere) at 11:59 PM Eastern Time (ET) on August 31, 2026.

This market resolves to NO if he has been released from physical custody at any point in that time.

"Released" includes being let out on bail, bond, personal recognizance, or having the extradition warrant/charges dismissed.

Being placed under house arrest, monitored by an ankle bracelet, or subjected to travel restrictions without being physically confined to a detention facility or jail will resolve to NO.

Resolution will be determined using credible, mainstream media reports (e.g., AP News, Reuters, BBC, TMZ) or official court/inmate records.

Background

On July 18, 2026, Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan were arrested by U.S. Marshals outside an event venue in Miami, Florida. The arrest was carried out on behalf of a UK extradition request following newly authorized charges by the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS). These expanded charges against Andrew Tate include seven counts of rape, three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, three counts of assault, and 19 charges relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.

The brothers, who are dual U.S.-British citizens, had arrived in Florida in February 2025 after Romanian prosecutors permitted them to leave Romania while awaiting trial there. They now face potential extradition proceedings in U.S. federal court to be returned to the UK.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-07-18: The question resolves on credible media reports (AP, Reuters, BBC, TMZ) or court and inmate records. TMZ's arrest article was the background source, and I could not open it. AP and NPR reported the same day that U.S. Marshals arrested Andrew and Tristan Tate in Miami on a sealed warrant. British prosecutors said they were seeking extradition on rape and trafficking charges covering 2010 to 2017: 59 charges in total, 42 of them against Andrew. [NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/07/18/g-s1-134475/tate-brothers-arrested-miami), [Michigan Public/AP](https://www.michiganpublic.org/2026-07-18/the-tate-brothers-are-arrested-in-miami-u-s-marshals-service-tells-ap)
- Latest status as of 2026-08-14: Andrew Tate is in federal detention in Miami, and no bail ruling has been made.

## 2. Current status
- In U.S. extradition cases the law presumes against bail. A defendant has to show "special circumstances" and also that he is not a flight risk or a danger to the community. [KTAR/AP](https://ktar.com/national-news/defense-attorneys-say-tate-brothers-should-remain-free-in-the-us-as-they-fight-extradition-to-the-uk)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)

[Washington Times/AP](https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2026/aug/13/tate-brothers-detention-hearing-postponed-aug-27-miami-extradition/), [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/judge-will-hear-tate-brothers-stay-custody-fight-uk-extradition-rcna592280), [PBS](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/nation/judge-postpones-hearing-over-whether-tate-brothers-should-stay-in-custody-as-they-fight-extradition)

They said they understood their rights, were held in federal detention afterward, and vowed to fight extradition. I found no detention ruling from that day. [Northeast Times](https://northeasttimes.com/2026/07/21/tate-brothers-appear-in-miami-court-vow-to-fight-uk-extradition/), [Gloucester Times/AP](https://www.gloucestertimes.com/news/national_world_news/tate-brothers-make-first-court-appearance-since-arrest-on-rape-and-sex-trafficking-charges/article_68aff1bb-6a1a-57be-b01b-dddb9bd8ea7f.html)

## 4. Base rates
- Because of the presumption against bail and the "special circumstances" test, people facing extradition from the U.S. are usually held in custody. I could not find a quantified rate.
- Bail hearings often end without a ruling on the day, and the judge issues a written decision later. With the hearing on August 27, a ruling and actual release would both have to happen within about 4 days to beat the deadline.
- Tate's own history:
  - **Romania, 2022 to 2023:** about 3 months in custody, followed by house arrest.
  - **UK, 2024:** arrested on a UK warrant, but the Romanian court ordered the UK extradition to happen only after the Romanian case ends. Bail was not the issue there.

- After the hearing: the judge could issue a written ruling, and either side could appeal to a district judge.
- Mid-September (per the Polymarket page text, not independently verified): the UK's deadline to submit its full extradition documents. This falls after the resolution date.

- Bail in U.S. extradition cases is generally granted rarely. I found no quantitative base rate.
